target_customer: Frontier AI labs buying agent training data, and companies licensing their internal work history
problem: Agents trained on simulated tasks lack real work; Ooak turns licensed anonymized company workflows into digital twin environments for training.
business_model: Data licensing to labs with revenue share style purchases from companies

founders.name: Thomas Aubry
education: Institut superieur de mecanique de Paris, Mechatronics and Robotics
founders.background_notes: A third cofounder, Gregoire, is named in the YC launch post, with no role or background given.

founders.name: Grégoire Lamy
founders.background_notes: YC launch post for Ooak Data names 3 cofounders: Pierre-Louis, Grégoire and Thomas (source https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/ooak-data); surname Lamy from CB Insights only.

competitors.name: Bespoke Labs
competitors.what: Training grounds and digital twins of enterprise systems for agents

competitors.name: Deeptune
competitors.what: Simulated enterprise workspaces for agent training

technical_complexity.rationale: Anonymizing real workflows and reconstructing consistent multi-tool company twins is hard, plus a two sided data acquisition problem.

defensibility.rationale: Licensed real workflow data from companies is exclusive and slow to collect, but labs have alternatives and may build in-house.

market_need_then: Analysts in 2026 describe heavy frontier lab demand for RL environments; one lab leader publicly doubted the startup category.

identity.voice_and_tone: Emphasizes real work, trust and anonymization

brand_strength.rationale: No brand press found; the name is hard to pronounce and the origin is unexplained.

outcome_analysis: Ooak Data is a Summer 2026 YC company with no outcome yet. Its differentiator is licensed real company workflow data, which is hard to collect, but it competes with funded environment startups and with data vendors in a crowded 2026 market.
notes: CB Insights lists $500K convertible note and Dealroom a $125k seed; unverified and matching the YC standard deal, so no round recorded. Founding year 2024 is from the YC page; CB Insights says September 2024 in France. Gregoire Lamy as cofounder comes from CB Insights summary and the YC launch post, not recorded as a founder entry. Completeness pass: a $500K convertible note with no date rests on a single database (CB Insights); Dealroom instead lists a $125K seed, a conflicting figure that is not summed or recorded. Co-founder Gregoire added from the YC launch post (3 cofounders named Pierre-Louis, Gregoire and Thomas); surname Lamy comes from CB Insights only.
